provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)
provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: The systematic review methodology does not follow published best practices for conducting systematic reviews, and the authors do not acknowledge this as a limitation; the evaluator considers this a major limitation of the work.
issues.quote:
Authors have not used published best-practices in the conduct of a systematic review, and have
not noted this as a limitation of the work.

issues.text: The paper uses causal language ('causal link', 'causal interpretation', 'effect of lead exposure') that the correlational study designs cannot support; the evaluator suggests framing results as associations or relationships instead.
issues.quote:
Phrases like 'causal link', 'causal interpretation' and 'effect of lead
exposure' do not seem appropriate given the study designs.

issues.text: Confounding by comorbidities and correlated factors such as socioeconomic status, which are also related to lower cognitive achievement, means the data cannot establish the causal claim made later in the manuscript.
issues.quote:
Despite arguing the causal
link later in the manuscript, the data itself cannot make this claim,
particularly when there are so many comorbidities to lead exposure that
are also related to lower cognitive achievement (e.g., SES).

issues.text: The search is described as aiming to identify all relevant studies, but only existing systematic reviews and Google Scholar were searched, so the search is not comprehensive and the authors must acknowledge this.
issues.quote:
Authors need to acknowledge the search is not comprehensive. They state
that they seek to identify "all studies measuring the correlation
between blood levels and IQ or test scores", but then report that only
existing SRs and Google Scholar were searched.

issues.text: The review needs a substantive limitations paragraph addressing the lack of duplicate independent full-text screening, duplicate risk-of-bias assessment, and discussion of publication bias in the underlying literature.
issues.quote:
There needs to be a robust paragraph about the limitations of the
systematic review methodology employed here.

issues.text: The paper does not state whether the search or inclusion was restricted by publication year or language, which the evaluator requests be reported.
issues.quote:
Please provide details on whether there were exclusions based on
publication year or language.

issues.text: The evaluator asks for the minimum and maximum number of effect estimates contributed by a single study, given 286 estimates from 47 studies.
issues.quote:
It would be useful to know the minimum and maximum
number of estimates contributed by a single study.

issues.text: Figures 3 and 4 lack the number of estimates averaged for each study and the actual weighted RVE average effect in the figure notes.
issues.quote:
In Figures 3 and 4, please add the number of estimates being averaged
for each study.

issues.text: The test of group differences between reading and math in Figure 4 is unexplained: it is unclear why it was included or why such a difference would be expected, and it is not discussed in the text.
issues.quote:
It is unclear why this test was included or why such a difference would
be expected. There is also no discussion of the test of group
differences in text.

issues.text: Figure A3 omits study citations, and the entry for Taylor (2017) appears surprising because it is a non-significant study with low weight yet is said to weaken the effect; the evaluator asks the authors to confirm it is the correct study.
issues.quote:
It is very surprising that
Taylor (2017)[@nwhm4rqutj5] would weaken the effect since it is a
non-significant study without a particularly high weight.

issues.text: A PRISMA flow chart is missing and should show each search phase and reasons for exclusion at full text.
issues.quote:
A PRISMA flow chart should be included to illustrate each phase of the
search process as well as the reasons for exclusion at full text.

issues.text: Appendix tables A1 and A2 lack key study characteristics such as sample size, age at lead and cognitive testing, and the cognitive measures used for reading and math.
issues.quote:
It would be useful to have additional information in A1 and A2, e.g.,
sample size, age at lead testing, age at cognitive testing, what was the
measure used for cognitive testing (for reading and math).

issues.text: The introduction does not give readers early context on blood lead levels in low, middle, and high income countries, so the results are hard to interpret before they are presented.
issues.quote:
It would be helpful to know, on average, what the
differences are in average blood lead levels for children in LICs vis a
vis MICs or HICs earlier in the intro

issues.text: The introduction's second sentence does not follow logically from the first: it references 3% from high-income countries, which were not mentioned, and it is unclear whether middle-income countries are meant.
issues.quote:
You state that 600 million children in
L&MICs have elevated blood lead levels, and then you state that 3% of
this comes from HIC

issues.text: The symbol sigma is used on the first page of the introduction without explanation as the standard deviation, which may confuse some readers.
issues.quote:
when sigma is first used
in the text (on page one of the intro) it may be useful to explain that
this is the symbol for standard deviation.

issues.text: Numbers 149 and 15 on page 31 lack units of measurement.
issues.quote:
please add the unit of measurement
for the 149 and 15 numbers.
